title: Speed, distance and time
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers speed = distance ÷ time with distance-time graphs; the closest ones, on calculus-based motion and on reading velocity from graphs, teach a different and deeper idea.

draft.title: Speed, distance and time
card: Speed = distance ÷ time. Rearranged, distance = speed × time and time = distance ÷ speed. Keep the units matching, such as km with hours.
Worked example: a cyclist rides 45 km in 3 hours. Speed = 45 ÷ 3 = 15 km/h. At 15 km/h, 20 km takes 20 ÷ 15 = 1.33 hours.
On a distance-time graph, time is across and distance is up. The gradient (rise ÷ run) is the speed, so a steeper line means a faster speed.
A flat line means distance is not changing, so the object is stopped. A line going back down towards zero means the object is returning to the start.
draft.remember: Speed = distance ÷ time, and on a distance-time graph the gradient is the speed.

a.q: A train travels 240 km at a steady speed of 80 km/h. How long does the trip take?
a.why: Time = distance ÷ speed = 240 ÷ 80 = 3 hours. Dividing speed by distance instead gives 0.33, which flips the rearranged formula.
a.clue: Time is distance divided by speed.

b.q: On a distance-time graph, Priya's line rises from 0 km at 0 h to 12 km at 2 h. It then stays flat until 3 h. What is her average speed over the first 2 hours, and what does the flat part show?
opts: 6 km/h, and she is moving slowly
4 km/h, and she is moving slowly
b.why: Speed is the gradient: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 km/h. A flat line means distance is not changing, so she is stopped, not moving slowly. Dividing by 3 hours gives 4 km/h, but the first stage lasts only 2 hours.
b.clue: Use only the first 2 hours, and ask what a gradient of zero means.
